A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sci2Pol work and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, references, and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite extensive relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 13 LLMs, fine-tuning experiments with three models, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds human evaluations, further robustness checks, and cross-domain generation case studies.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, retrieval/filtering/polishing pipeline, scoring rubrics, and LoRA fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. Alternative exemplars and MiniMax-M2 are tested in supplementary controls rather than adopted as revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds exploratory full-brief generation using one paper each about AI governance, public-space robotics, mathematics education, financial inclusion, and scientific uptake in policy. This substantially broadens evaluated subject matter, although evidence within each added domain is limited to one case.

E2.justification: v2 adds two human performance baselines covering sampled questions from all 18 tasks, presented alongside Grok-3-beta in Table 14. These introduce a human reference absent from v1; the original 13-model comparison roster remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include subsampled human task evaluation, human scoring of ten cases per selected task, repolishing with three different exemplars, evaluation on eight new pairs, and constructor/judge substitutions for Tasks 11 and 13. Original task metrics, training split, LoRA settings, and hardware remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's retained analyses, v2 adds direct human validation, qualitative SFT comparisons, two additional leakage checks, MiniMax-M2 construction/judging controls, model-size/compute/date analyses, and cross-domain case studies. These substantially expand scrutiny of reliability and generalization.

E5.justification: Both retain 1,000 bootstrap iterations with seed 42 and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting. v2 newly reports 100% agreement between two annotation reviewers, averages two human scorers, and explicitly omits bootstrap testing for its small human studies.

E6.justification: Original results in Tables 2, 3, 8, and 9 are unchanged. Numerous supplementary results are added, including human scores, alternative-constructor/judge results, and qualitative comparisons. On the eight new Task 15 pairs, Table 29 reports 83.21 for Gemma-3-27B-SFT versus 81.02 for its base model; these are additional test-set results.

T1.justification: The scoring definitions and formulas in v1 Appendix I and v2 Appendix L are retained. No substantive theorem, proof, or derivation is added; the new FLOPs heuristic supports an empirical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: an 18-task benchmark, a 639-pair training corpus, evaluation of 13 LLMs, and fine-tuning gains including Gemma-27B surpassing GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3 overall. The expanded conclusion largely restates these contributions.

C2.justification: Sections H.3–H.4 add extensive interpretations of failure modes and attribute SFT benefits to factual grounding, style, structural patterns, and implicit skills. H.11 interprets scaling relationships, Appendix I argues for cross-domain generalization, and D.1 newly identifies multi-source policy synthesis as outside the work's scope.

D1.justification: v2 adds source DOIs, venues, and access dates; documents CC-BY-NC 4.0 licensing and a metadata/controlled-excerpt release protocol; and expands annotation and reproducibility disclosures. Existing training configurations, hardware information, dataset links, and substantive prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds policy-LLM references such as Coz et al. and Bai et al. (2025), plus source works supporting the new evaluations. The related-work discussion and positioning against SciRIFF, MMLU-Pro, and Political-LLM remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the document: it removes the front contents section, places references before the appendices, moves key experimental findings to G.2 and broader impact to D.2, expands the conclusion, and introduces dedicated reproducibility, LLM-usage, and dataset-link sections. Much of the methodological prose remains verbatim.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the ICLR layout, revises Figure 1, and adds Figure 4 and numerous validation and case-study tables. Existing long comparisons are consolidated, including v1 Tables 16–19 into v2 Tables 24–25 and v1 Tables 23–26 into v2 Tables 32–33.

improvement.justification: The additional exemplar-replacement, new-pair, and alternative-constructor/judge checks strengthen validation beyond v1, while human scoring and provenance disclosures improve assessability. However, small samples limit generalization, H.6.1's claim of consistent superiority contradicts Table 19, and Table 20 pairs an Indigenous-research passage with coastal-barrier summaries. These reporting problems limit the net quality gain.
